reasoning: Both sets are disciplined, graph-shaped plans with frozen contracts, entry sketches, task packets and dependency tables, and both make the same mistakes on the user's stated choices: SSE instead of WebSocket, and Nasdaq Data Link instead of Sharadar's own API. Each also drops one explicit requirement. Set B has no Yahoo/yahooquery cross-check and no trace of the user's 10 delisted names; its validation only checks against Sharadar's own closeadj. Set A pushes PPO agents out of S4 into an unplanned 'later idea', and its S4 idea file falsely says the brief forbids cloud compute, when the user rents GPUs. A does better on the rest of S1: its M1 is a richer vertical slice (start a download from the app, watch live progress, find the delisted company, open the universe page), and its spec carries the cross-check and the reference delisted list. A also ships CONSTRAINTS.md, which every packet in both sets tells the builder to read and which B does not have. A's roadmap ties each reference file to a milestone (RF-01 to M4/M6, RF-02/03 to M8), and every milestone has its own outline, skills and references. B is better in some places: a brief that covers all stages (learning goal, GPU, a ledger for every claim), PPO included, and many golden cases for M1 (TC-01–27), where A's qdata has no golden cases at all. B's later milestones, though, are one-line outlines with no Skills or References, and B adds sources nobody asked for (EDGAR, FRED). Overall A fits the user's data-trust goals and is easier to build from, so A wins narrowly.
